name: farkle-r2
context:
ROUND 2. You returned REVISE on four counts. Three are accepted and fixed; one I measured before accepting, and the measurement supports you more strongly than your own wording did.

─────────── YOUR CENTRAL FINDING, MEASURED ───────────

You wrote: 'the transition from rolling 6 dice to selecting 6 dice from 36 fundamentally breaks the risk/reward loop... the probability of a player being unable to find a connected path of length <= 6 that contains at least one 1 or 5 is statistically negligible. This transforms Farkle from a game of managing risk into a game of maximizing efficiency.'

I did not take this on authority. I built the exhaustive path search — every connected simple path of length <= 6 from every cell, scored through the real Farkle table — and ran it over 400 seeded boards.

    FRESH BOARDS WITH NO SCORING PATH: 0 / 400 = 0.00%

So 'statistically negligible' is too kind. It is ZERO. A player on a fresh board cannot farkle even by trying. The loss condition in a push-your-luck game never fires, which means there is no push and no luck — exactly your finding, and worse than stated.

─────────── THE FIX, AND WHY IT IS THE TABLETOP STRUCTURE ───────────

The defect was not 'selecting from 36'. It was REFILLING between selections. Tabletop Farkle's whole engine is that you set the scorers aside and reroll THE REST: each continuation has fewer dice, so farkle probability climbs, and that climb is the decision.

The grid analogue is exact. Within a turn, scored cells CLEAR AND DO NOT REFILL. The board fragments, connectivity dies, and the next chain gets harder. Refill happens only after the player banks or farkles.

Measured, same 400 boards, a greedy continuation policy:

    step 1   0.0%      step 7   20.4%
    step 2   0.0%      step 8   46.8%
    step 3   0.0%      step 9   63.1%
    step 4   0.0%      step 10  91.5%
    step 5   0.3%      step 11  100.0%
    step 6   5.3%

That is a push-your-luck curve with a real shape: four free continuations, tension arriving around step 5-6, and a cliff past 8. It matches the tabletop feel, where the first rolls are safe and the fear arrives as dice leave the table. Nothing was tuned to produce it — it falls out of connectivity dying on a 36-cell grid, which is a fact about the board rather than a number somebody picked.

One consequence I want on the record rather than buried: a player who banks at step 3 is taking no risk at all, so the early game is a formality. Whether that is pacing or padding is a real open question and I have not resolved it.

─────────── YOUR OTHER THREE FINDINGS ───────────

(d) THE WILDCARD CONTRADICTION — ACCEPTED, FEATURE CUT. You found that idea 30 (wildcards are fallible claims resolved at chain close) and idea 21 (the preview uses the same lookupScore the executor uses) are mutually exclusive: 'you cannot have a certain preview for an uncertain wildcard.' Correct and unanswerable. Wildcards are CUT from v1. The preview/executor identity is load-bearing — it is what stops a client showing a number the server will disagree with — and a cosmetic feature does not get to break it.

(b) COOP IS CORROSIVE — ACCEPTED, REDESIGNED. You called the shared unbanked pot a Stag Hunt where 'the safe player will feel held hostage by the risky player.' I think that is right and the hostage dynamic is the specific failure. The shared resource is now THE BOARD, NOT THE SCORE. Two players, one board, alternating turns, SEPARATE banks. Cells one player clears are gone for the other. Cooperation is spatial: taking a chain out of the middle can strand your partner's region, and a good pair carves the board so both keep options. Nobody can lose anybody else's points, so there is nothing to resent — but the board is genuinely shared, so it is not two solo games summed either.

(e) THE DEGENERATE STRATEGY — ACCEPTED AS THE GATE. You named greedy path-based EV maximisation and said to measure FARKLE FREQUENCY, failing the design if it drops below about 5%. That becomes a hard pass condition in this game's Monte Carlo harness, alongside the skill spread. I will also report the frequency PER STEP rather than pooled, since the table above shows a pooled figure would average a 0% region against a 91% one and mean nothing.

(c) You said transparency raises the ceiling because the question becomes EV-per-path rather than guessing. Kept unchanged: the pay table is published and combos are named.

─────────── WHAT CHANGES IN THE 52 ───────────

SUPERSEDED: 6 (hot dice as a bonus) — continuation is now the core loop, not a reward. 13/14 (refill during a turn) — refill is between turns only. 30 (wildcards) — cut. 34/35 (shared pot coop) — replaced by shared board, separate banks.

ADDED: 53 the turn ends when the player banks OR no scoring chain remains. 54 the board is NOT refilled mid-turn, and this is the rule the whole risk curve rests on. 55 the per-step farkle probability is shown to the player as the forecast strip's row-2 confidence — the strip now forecasts RISK rather than faces, which is a better fit for this game than for the lattice. 56 a turn that reaches step 8+ is visibly rare and the interface says so. 57 solo, vs and coop all share this turn structure.

UNCHANGED AND STILL PROPOSED: everything in rules/scoring except 6, the cascade and gravity rules for BETWEEN turns, bombs 23-29, modes 31-33 and 36-38, forecast 39-45 as amended by 55, and the whole visual identity block 46-52 (pip tokens through the 4D projection, amber axis, chain as a ribbon, combo named not numbered).

─────────── STILL NOT MEASURED ───────────

The skill spread between a random, greedy and search agent. Whether the amber/cyan/magenta split survives at launcher thumbnail size. Whether four free continuations is pacing or padding.

questions.text: Clearing without refill inside a turn produces a measured farkle curve of 0% for four steps then 5%, 20%, 47%, 63%, 92%. Is that the right shape for a push-your-luck game, or are the four risk-free steps at the start dead time that should be compressed?
Coop is now a shared board with separate banks, where clearing a chain can strand your partner. Is that genuine cooperation, or is it just competition over a common pool wearing a coop label?

Idea 55 repurposes the forecast strip's second row to show farkle RISK rather than upcoming faces. Does a forecast of your own probability of failure help a player decide, or does it remove the judgement that was the point?
I cut wildcards rather than weaken the preview/executor identity. Was that the right trade, or is there a formulation of a wildcard that keeps both?
Name the strongest remaining reason this design would fail playtest.
